question: The amount on a sum of ₹4,400 at the rate of 20% per annum compound interest, compounded annually, in 2 years will be:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net percentage change for 2 years at 20% = 20 + 20 + (20 × 20) ÷ 100 = 44%

Total amount percentage = 100% (Principal) + 44% (Interest) = 144%

Required Amount = 4400 × 144%

Amount = 44 × 144 = 6336

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6,336.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹4,400

Rate (R) = 20% per annum

Time (n) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + R ÷ 100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dd6fa77fc8d051db8a5ff4a75e50f39df97fb2bfc7fcb00081b0fd8f065a1f30.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ A = 4400 × (1 + 20 ÷ 100)²

⇒ A = 4400 × (1 + 1 ÷ 5)²

⇒ A = 4400 × (6 ÷ 5)²

⇒ A = 4400 × (36 ÷ 25)

⇒ A = 176 × 36

⇒ A = 6336

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6,336.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Interest Rate

For a rate of r% for 2 years, the effective compound interest rate is calculated as r + r + (r × r) ÷ 100.

CI vs SI Difference

The difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest for 2 years is given by P × (R ÷ 100)².

Compounding Periods

If interest is compounded half-yearly, the rate becomes R ÷ 2 and the time period becomes 2n in the formula A = P(1 + R ÷ 100)ⁿ.
